text.title: Competitive Intelligence Methods Core Rules
text.summary: Seven rules for choosing and operating CI collection methods: signal-to-method mapping, the legal and ethical line between public-source collection and pretexting, the false-signal mode each method must declare, automated-collection limits, and what a collection plan must name.

rule.statement: `methods_selected` is derived from the `signal_needed` value through an explicit mapping, and each selected row names the field it produces: pricing → pricing-page diff + published reseller/partner rate card; roadmap → changelog, release notes, public issue tracker, conference talks; hires → job-board diff; funding → registry filings (SEC EDGAR, Companies House) + press; churn → review-site movement and "switched from" mentions; positioning → homepage copy diff + public ad libraries.

rationale.source: SCIP intelligence cycle — planning and direction stage precedes collection

rule.rationale: Analysts default to whatever collector they already own. A scraper pointed at the wrong surface returns a large, clean dataset that answers a question nobody asked, and the volume of it is mistaken for coverage.

rule.statement: Any human-source method — competitor sales call, customer-call probe, conference conversation, ex-employee interview — requires the collector to state real name and employer before the conversation. Posing as a prospect, student, journalist, analyst or job applicant is forbidden; such a method must be listed in `methods_rejected` with reason `pretexting`.

rationale.source: SCIP Code of Ethics — disclose all relevant information, including one's identity and organisation, prior to all interviews

rule.rationale: Pretexted collection is unusable at the point it matters: it cannot be cited to a board or to counsel, so the finding cannot support the decision it was gathered for. Where the pretext induces disclosure of protected information it also moves the collection into trade-secret misappropriation territory (US Economic Espionage Act, 18 U.S.C. §1832).

rule.statement: Collection is limited to surfaces reachable without credentials and without accepting the competitor's customer terms: public pages, published filings, public repositories, job boards, review sites, ad libraries. Trial signups under a false company, scraping behind authentication, and material carried in by a new hire under NDA are rejected methods.

rationale.source: Van Buren v. United States (2021) + hiQ Labs v. LinkedIn (9th Cir. 2022)

rule.rationale: Those decisions narrowed the CFAA around genuinely public pages but left access past an authentication gate squarely inside the statute. The defensible line is therefore the login wall, not the word "scraping" — and a method that crosses it makes every downstream artefact undisclosable.

rule.statement: Every selected method has a matching `false_signal_guards` row naming its known false signal and the check that clears it. Minimum set: pricing-page diff → split test or geo-localised price; review-site scrape → vendor-run incentivised review campaign; hiring-signal → backfill or never-filled req; GitHub-velocity → mirror repo or dependency bump commits; patent-pull → defensive filing never productised.

rationale.source: Internal — false-signal catalogue per collection method

rule.rationale: Each collection surface has a dominant artefact that looks exactly like the signal being hunted. Because the artefact is generated by a routine process, it recurs every cycle, so an unguarded method produces a steady stream of confident false positives rather than an occasional one.

rule.statement: Any automated method declares the robots.txt user-agent group it obeys and its request rate; a collector that ignores `Disallow` or exceeds roughly 1 request/second per host is rejected in favour of the manual variant of the same method.
rule.rationale: RFC 9309 makes robots.txt the operator's machine-readable access policy, so ignoring it converts defensible public-source collection into an access dispute. The practical failure comes first: the IP range gets blocked, and the time series the CI programme depends on truncates silently mid-cycle.

rule.statement: `collection_plan` states, per selected method: cadence, one named human (not a team alias), and the storage path where the RAW capture lands — not the summary. A method with no raw-capture path is rejected.
rule.rationale: Next cycle's diff needs something to diff against. With only summaries retained, the analyst compares a summary to a summary and each pass loses detail, so drift accumulates invisibly and the first genuine change is indistinguishable from accumulated paraphrase.

rule.statement: Emit a structured skip when: the needed signal has exactly one lawful source (just collect it, no selection artefact required); the programme has no recurring cadence, so a one-shot competitor-analysis is the right artefact; or every candidate method fails `identity-disclosed-no-pretexting` or `collection-stops-at-the-login-wall` — in which case the skip records the legal reason instead of a degraded plan.

rationale.source: Methodology boundary — this methodology selects methods; competitive-intelligence operates them

rule.rationale: A selection artefact with one candidate documents a decision that was never made, and reviewers later read it as evidence that alternatives were weighed. Where the blocker is legal, the skip record is the only durable trace that the method was considered and refused.
